cases.title: The Offseason: Rebuilding Around Haliburton's Return
cases.context: Standing case for a team that made the 2025 NBA Finals and lost its floor general seven minutes into Game 7: Tyrese Haliburton ruptured his Achilles in that game, costing him the entire 2025-26 season. Recovery has been the defining storyline since - he's back to 5-on-5 work (a shingles diagnosis briefly slowed the ramp-up), and the organization has voiced confidence he's a Day 1 option for 2026-27, but every step of that timeline is news. The roster around him changed while he was out: Indiana sent Isaiah Jackson and Bennedict Mathurin (plus draft capital) to the Clippers for Kobe Brown and Ivica Zubac, later flipped Kam Jones to the Bulls for Braden Smith, re-signed Brown and Jalen Slawson, and added veteran Larry Nance Jr. - a real shift from the pace-and-space identity that got them to the Finals. Indiana also gave up its own 2026 first-round pick in an earlier deal, limiting draft flexibility this cycle. Track: Haliburton's health and ramp-up, whether Zubac at center changes the offensive identity, and whether a wounded-but-recent-Finalist holds position in a crowded East heading into camp.
